testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, how should you begin?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction you want to go.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is true about broken suspension parts?
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up your vehicle and load and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. It is especially important to check mirrors when turning, changing lanes, merging, and doing tight maneuvers.

questions.question: In very hot weather, air pressure in tires decreases.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire air pressure increases in very hot weather. Stop often to check your tires and make sure they don't overheat or blow out.

questions.question: When hauling a heavy load with spring brakes, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle will need more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: Which gas from a faulty exhaust system is dangerous?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas, enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control speed. Use your brakes only to help the engine braking.

questions.question: If the air compressor has a belt, what should be checked?
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor belt. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor stops working.
Only hold air during an emergency.
Hold air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for you to brake several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. Try to find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: Dual tires should:

options.text: Both be in contact with the road surface.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle, check that your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only ahead and to the right.
Look ahead, to the sides, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead, to the sides, and behind.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening all around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, the S-cam:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Presses the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, it presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If transporting 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, you must use a minimum of ____ to secure it.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Any cargo must be secured with a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: If you must stop on a one-way or divided highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.explanation: If you stop on a one-way or divided highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo:

options.text: Reduces stress on the trailer frame.
Is unsafe, but unlikely to damage the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safety. Unsecured cargo can fall and cause injury or death. Poor loading can damage the vehicle and make steering difficult.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift to a low gear. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go downhill.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: A truck may need to stay below the legal maximum weight when driving:
questions.explanation: In some driving conditions, it is not safe to operate at full legal weight. Be mindful of this in poor weather and on mountainous roads.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a motorist on the side of the road

questions.explanation: Accident scenes are hazardous because people may not watch for traffic and can distract other drivers. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children who may not pay attention to vehicles. People near the roadway often focus on stores instead of traffic.

questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: It only happens at very high speeds.
It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
It happens most often when tire pressure is too high.
It happens most often when tires have good tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely to happen if tire pressure is too low or if tire tread is worn.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.explanation: You should cover cargo to protect people from spilled cargo and to protect cargo from weather. Keeping cargo secret is not a reason to cover it.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not apply the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain traction.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It distracts you both mentally and physically.
A message may upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts you both mentally and physically.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction. It takes your mind off the road and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: When should mirrors be used?

options.text: By a helper to watch blind spots.

questions.explanation: You should check the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle frequently while driving.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually to make sure your vehicle stops smoothly and safely.

questions.question: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit, oil, coolant, and anti-lock braking system (ABS) lights.

questions.question: When must a written vehicle inspection report be signed?

options.text: Only if defects were found and repaired.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a law enforcement officer asks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repaired.
questions.explanation: You must sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and certified as repaired or not needing repair.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To prevent other drivers from seeing what is being transported

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent other drivers from seeing what is being transported
questions.explanation: You should cover cargo to protect people from spilled cargo and to protect cargo from weather. Hiding cargo from other drivers is not a reason to cover it.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you go downhill.

questions.question: On low bridges:

options.text: Height warnings must always be posted.
Height warnings must be posted at least twice.
Height warnings may be posted, but they don't have to be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Height warnings may be posted, but they don't have to be.
questions.explanation: Height warnings are often posted on low bridges, but not always. If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection:

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report must only be reviewed if passengers will ride in the vehicle.
You should review the last inspection report, if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should review the last inspection report, if one exists.
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to review the last inspection report. Only sign the report if you have repaired any problems that were noted.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle parked:

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if your brakes are wet and it is freezing outside.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection:

options.text: Should be done the same way every time.
Should be done differently every time.
Does not always need to include all items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't forget to check something.

questions.question: The driver is responsible for safely transporting cargo.
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe cargo transport, no matter who loaded the vehicle.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, you must place warning devices within 10 minutes. What should you place?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave at passing traffic.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the roadside, place emergency warning devices like reflective triangles within 10 minutes.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS is not working, your basic brakes still work, so you can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: Why are roads slippery when it first starts to rain?

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts because the water mixes with oil and grease on the road, creating a slippery surface. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should a driver do?

options.text: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, pull forward straight first. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be completely within the parking space.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, if your route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain what you would do at a simulated crossing location.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control which system?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: What should you know about lights you see while driving in fog?

options.text: You can assume the lights are on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is. A vehicle may have left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. A vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, you cannot rely on lights to show where the road is. The lights may come from a vehicle that has driven off the road.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safety of cargo in a vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver can load cargo.
Another person can load cargo and is responsible for its safety.
Another person can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
Only a shipping company employee can load cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another person can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
questions.explanation: No matter who loads the cargo, the driver is always responsible for keeping it safe and secure.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is what you use during normal driving. It applies and releases brakes when you press the brake pedal.

questions.question: How long is a CDL valid?
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, a CDL is valid for five years from the date it is issued.

questions.question: What should be done with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Use them on the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic.
When vehicles are too close together.

questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver changes lanes or turns too quickly.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.
